title: Find X Value of Array I
summary: Given an array of positive integers nums and a positive integer k, you can remove any non-overlapping prefix and suffix in one operation.
statement: Given an array of positive integers nums and a positive integer k, you can remove any non-overlapping prefix and suffix in one operation. Calculate the x-value for each x from 0 to k-1, where x is the number of ways to perform the operation such that the product of the remaining elements leaves a remainder of x when divided by k. Return an array of size k with the x-values.
constraints: nums has up to 100,000 positive integers and 1 <= k <= 5.
Removing a prefix and suffix while leaving a nonempty array is equivalent to choosing a nonempty contiguous subarray.
For every remainder 0 through k-1, return how many subarray products have that remainder modulo k.
reference_solution:
def count_subarray_product_remainders(nums,k):
    answer=[0]*k;ending=[0]*k
    for value in nums:
        current=[0]*k;current[value%k]+=1
        for remainder,count in enumerate(ending):current[remainder*value%k]+=count
        for remainder,count in enumerate(current):answer[remainder]+=count
        ending=current
    return answer

def count_subarray_product_remainders(nums,k):
    answer=[0]*k;ending=[0]*k
    for value in nums:
        current=[0]*k;current[value%k]+=1
        for remainder,count in enumerate(ending):current[(remainder+value)%k]+=count
        for remainder,count in enumerate(current):answer[remainder]+=count
        ending=current
    return answer
hints: Every retained array is a contiguous subarray, so count product remainders for all subarrays.
Maintain counts by remainder for subarrays ending at the previous position, then extend them by the new value.
Start the one-value subarray, multiply every prior ending remainder, add current counts to the global result, and advance.
Each subarray is created exactly once at its right endpoint, and modular multiplication preserves precisely the needed state.
